controls.description: In this chapter:
"Breach of system security" has the meaning 	assigned by Section 521.053.
"Exemplary damages" has the meaning assigned by 	Section 41.001, Civil Practice and Remedies Code.
"Personal identifying information" and "sensitive 	personal information" have the meanings assigned by Section 	521.002.
This chapter 	applies only to a business entity in this state that:
has fewer than 250 employees; and
owns or licenses computerized data that includes 	sensitive personal information.

Notwithstanding any other law, in an action 	arising from a breach of system security, a person harmed as a 	result of the breach may not recover exemplary damages from a 	business entity to which this chapter applies if the entity 	demonstrates that at the time of the breach the entity implemented 	and maintained a cybersecurity program in compliance with Section 	542.004.
Cybersecurity Program Requirements

controls.title: 542.004(a)
controls.description: For purposes of 	Section 542.003, a cybersecurity program must:

controls.title: 542.004(a)(1)
controls.description: contain administrative, technical, and physical 	safeguards for the protection of personal identifying information 	and sensitive personal information;

controls.title: 542.004(a)(2)
controls.description: conform to an industry-recognized cybersecurity 	framework as described by Subsection (b);

controls.title: 542.004(a)(3)
controls.description: be designed to:

controls.title: 542.004(a)(3)(A)
controls.description: protect the security of personal identifying 	information and sensitive personal information;

controls.title: 542.004(a)(3)(B)
controls.description: protect against any threat or hazard to the 	integrity of personal identifying information and sensitive 	personal information; and

controls.title: 542.004(a)(3)(C)
controls.description: protect against unauthorized access to or 	acquisition of personal identifying information and sensitive 	personal information that would result in a material risk of 	identity theft or other fraud to the individual to whom the 	information relates; and

controls.title: 542.004(a)(4)
controls.description: with regard to the scale and scope, meet the 	following requirements:

controls.title: 542.004(a)(4)(A)
controls.description: for a business entity with fewer than 20 	employees, simplified requirements, including password policies 	and appropriate employee cybersecurity training;

controls.title: 542.004(a)(4)(B)
controls.description: for a business entity with at least 20 	employees but fewer than 100 employees, moderate requirements, 	including the requirements of the Center for Internet Security 	Controls Implementation Group 1; and

controls.title: 542.004(a)(4)(C)
controls.description: for a business entity with at least 100 	employees but fewer than 250 employees, compliance with the 	requirements of Subsection (b).

controls.title: 542.004(b)
controls.description: A cybersecurity program under this section conforms to 	an industry-recognized cybersecurity framework for purposes of 	this section if the program conforms to:

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)
controls.description: a current version of or any combination of current 	versions of the following:

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(A)
controls.description: the Framework for Improving Critical 	Infrastructure Cybersecurity published by the National Institute 	of Standards and Technology (NIST);

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(B)
controls.description: the NIST's special publication 800-171;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(C)
controls.description: the NIST's special publications 800-53 and 	800-53a;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(D)
controls.description: the Federal Risk and Authorization 	Management Program's FedRAMP Security Assessment Framework;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(E)
controls.description: the Center for Internet Security Critical 	Security Controls for Effective Cyber Defense;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(F)
controls.description: the ISO/IEC 27000-series information 	security standards published by the International Organization for 	Standardization and the International Electrotechnical Commission;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(G)
controls.description: the Health Information Trust Alliance's 	Common Security Framework;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(H)
controls.description: the Secure Controls Framework;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(I)
controls.description: the Service Organization Control Type 2 	Framework; or

controls.title: 542.004(b)(1)(J)
controls.description: other similar frameworks or standards of the 	cybersecurity industry;

controls.title: 542.004(b)(2)
controls.description: if the business entity is subject to its 	requirements, the current version of the following:

controls.title: 542.004(b)(2)(A)
controls.description: the Health Insurance Portability and 	Accountability Act of 1996 (42 U.S.C. Section 1320d et seq.);

controls.title: 542.004(b)(2)(B)
controls.description: Title V, Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (15 U.S.C. 	Section 6801 et seq.);

controls.title: 542.004(b)(2)(C)
controls.description: the Federal Information Security 	Modernization Act of 2014 (Pub. L. No. 113-283); or

controls.title: 542.004(b)(2)(D)
controls.description: the Health Information Technology for 	Economic and Clinical Health Act (Division A, Title XIII, and 	Division B, Title IV, Pub. L. No. 111-5); and

controls.title: 542.004(b)(3)
controls.description: if applicable to the business entity, a current 	version of the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard.

controls.title: 542.004(c)
controls.description: If any standard described by Subsection (b)(1) is 	published and updated, a business entity's cybersecurity program 	continues to meet the requirements of a program under this section 	if the entity updates the program to meet the updated standard not 	later than the later of:

controls.title: 542.004(c)(1)
controls.description: the implementation date published in the updated 	standard; or

controls.title: 542.004(c)(2)
controls.description: the first anniversary of the date on which the 	updated standard is published.
This chapter may not be construed to limit the authority of the 	attorney general to seek any legal or equitable remedy under the 	laws of this state.
This chapter does not affect the certification of an action as a 	class action.
